records.literal_gloss: And answered Job the LORD and said:

en.L: And Job answered {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and said:

es.L: Y respondió Job {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} y dijo:

fr.L: Et Job répondit {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} et dit :
fr.R: Alors Job a dit {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} :

pt.L: E Jó respondeu {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}} e disse:

decisions.choice: Job's second answer to the LORD
decisions.reason: After the first speech Job answered briefly and said he would speak no more (40:3-5). Now, after the second speech (40:6-41:26), he answers again. As with the other speech introductions, these words are prose and the answer (42:2-6) is poetry.

decisions.choice: answered (B), said to (R), without "and said"
decisions.reason: Hebrew introduces speech with two verbs; Literal keeps both, and Balanced and Readable say it once, as in the other speech introductions of Job (40:3).

decisions.choice: Narrative tenses: passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("répondit"), passé composé at Readable ("a dit"); Job's answer (42:2-6) is speech
decisions.reason: As in Job 1-2 and the speech introductions; the epilogue (42:7-17) follows the same rule.

decisions.choice: Job speaks to God in 합쇼체 with 주님 and 저 (42:2-6); God speaks to Eliphaz and his friends in 해라체 with 너, 너희 (42:7-8)
decisions.reason: The speech levels the terms for Job settle: Job to God as the psalmists pray, God to people as in the prophets.

source.text: יָ֭דַעְתִּי כִּי־כֹ֣ל תּוּכָ֑ל וְלֹא־יִבָּצֵ֖ר מִמְּךָ֣ מְזִמָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: I know that everything you are able [to do], and not is withheld from you a purpose.

en.L: I know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are able [to do] everything, \q and no purpose is withheld from {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.B: I know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} can do everything; \q no purpose of {{deity_pronoun:yours|Yours}} can be stopped.
en.R: I know that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} can do anything. \q No one can stop {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} plans.

es.L: Sé que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} puedes [hacerlo] todo, \q y ningún propósito {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} es vedado.
es.B: Sé que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} lo puedes todo; \q ningún propósito {{deity_pronoun:tuyo|Tuyo}} puede ser frustrado.
es.R: Sé que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} puedes hacer cualquier cosa. \q Nadie puede detener {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} planes.

fr.L: Je sais que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} peux [faire] toute chose, \q et qu’aucun projet ne {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}est impossible.
fr.B: Je sais que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} peux tout faire ; \q aucun de {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} desseins ne peut être arrêté.
fr.R: Je sais que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} peux tout faire. \q Personne ne peut empêcher {{deity_pronoun:tes|Tes}} projets.

sw.L: Najua kwamba {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} waweza [kufanya] kila kitu, \q wala hakuna kusudi linalozuiliwa {{deity_pronoun:kwako|Kwako}}.
sw.B: Najua ya kuwa {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} waweza kufanya yote; \q hakuna kusudi {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}} linaloweza kuzuiliwa.
sw.R: Najua kwamba {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} unaweza kufanya lolote. \q Hakuna mtu awezaye kuzuia mipango {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}.

vi.L: Con biết rằng Chúa có thể [làm] mọi sự, \q và không ý định nào của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bị ngăn trở.
vi.B: Con biết rằng Chúa làm được mọi việc; \q không ý định nào của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} có thể bị ngăn cản.
vi.R: Con biết Chúa có thể làm bất cứ điều gì. \q Không ai ngăn được kế hoạch của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 저는 주님께서 모든 것을 하실 수 있음을 압니다. \q 주님께는 어떤 뜻도 막히는 것이 없습니다.
ko.B: 저는 주님께서 무엇이든 하실 수 있음을 압니다. \q 주님의 뜻은 무엇도 가로막을 수 없습니다.
ko.R: 주님은 무엇이든 하실 수 있다는 것을 저는 압니다. \q 아무도 주님의 계획을 막을 수 없습니다.

pt.L: Eu sei que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} és capaz de [fazer] tudo, \q e nenhum propósito {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} é vedado.
pt.B: Eu sei que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} podes fazer todas as coisas; \q nenhum propósito {{deity_pronoun:teu|Teu}} pode ser impedido.
pt.R: Eu sei que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} podes fazer qualquer coisa. \q Ninguém pode impedir os {{deity_pronoun:teus|Teus}} planos.

decisions.choice: I know (as read)
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text spell "you know"; the scribes' reading note, followed by the word data and by nearly all translations, gives "I know". Job is confessing what he has now learned.

decisions.choice: no purpose is withheld from you: nothing God plans is beyond his power
decisions.reason: The same verb and noun are used in Genesis 11:6, where the LORD says that nothing the builders of Babel plan will be withheld from them. What was a danger in human hands is simply true of God.

decisions.choice: purpose: God's plan
decisions.reason: The noun usually means a scheme or plot, often a bad one (21:27). Of God it is his considered purpose, the "counsel" of 38:2 and 42:3 that Job now sees he could not grasp.

decisions.choice: Job to God: "Chúa" and "Ngài" for "you", "con" for himself
decisions.reason: As in his first reply (40:4-5) and the Psalms' prayers; here Job yields, and "con" fits his humbled words.

decisions.choice: Eu sei que tu és capaz de [fazer] tudo (L), podes fazer todas as coisas (B); nenhum propósito te é vedado (L)
decisions.reason: Drafted from the Hebrew, not from a familiar version: Literal keeps the verb "be able" and the passive "is withheld" (m2). "Tu" is written out, as in Job's earlier turns to God (9:28; 30:20), since his whole answer is now addressed to God.

source.text: מִ֤י זֶ֨ה׀מַעְלִ֥ים עֵצָ֗ה בְּֽלִ֫י דָ֥עַת לָכֵ֣ן הִ֭גַּדְתִּי וְלֹ֣א אָבִ֑ין נִפְלָא֥וֹת מִ֝מֶּ֗נִּי וְלֹ֣א אֵדָֽע׃

records.literal_gloss: Who [is] this hiding counsel without knowledge? Therefore I have declared and not I understood, [things] too wonderful for me, and not I knew.

en.L: Who [is] this who hides counsel without knowledge? \q Therefore I have spoken, and I did not understand, \q [things] too wonderful for me, which I did not know.
en.B: You asked, "Who is this who hides {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} plan without knowledge?" \q Truly I have spoken of what I did not understand, \q things too wonderful for me, which I did not know.
en.R: You asked, "Who is this who hides {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} plans by talking without knowing?" \q It is true: I talked about things I did not understand, \q things too wonderful for me to know.

es.L: ¿Quién [es] este que oculta el designio sin conocimiento? \q Por eso he hablado, y no entendía, \q [cosas] demasiado maravillosas para mí, que no conocía.
es.B: Tú preguntaste: «¿Quién es este que oculta {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} plan sin conocimiento?». \q En verdad hablé de lo que no entendía, \q de cosas demasiado maravillosas para mí, que yo no conocía.
es.R: Tú preguntaste: «¿Quién es este que oculta {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} planes hablando sin saber?». \q Es cierto: hablé de cosas que no entendía, \q cosas demasiado maravillosas para que yo las conociera.

fr.L: Qui [est] celui-ci qui cache le dessein sans connaissance ? \q C’est pourquoi j’ai parlé, et je ne comprenais pas, \q [des choses] trop merveilleuses pour moi, que je ne connaissais pas.
fr.B: Tu as demandé : « Qui est celui-ci qui cache {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} projet sans rien connaître ? » \q Oui, j’ai parlé de ce que je ne comprenais pas, \q de choses trop merveilleuses pour moi, que je ne connaissais pas.
fr.R: Tu as demandé : « Qui est celui-là qui cache {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} plans en parlant sans savoir ? » \q C’est vrai : j’ai parlé de choses que je ne comprenais pas, \q de choses trop merveilleuses pour que je les connaisse.

sw.L: Ni nani huyu anayeficha shauri bila maarifa? \q Kwa hiyo nimesema, wala sikuelewa, \q [mambo] ya ajabu mno kwangu, ambayo sikuyajua.
sw.B: Wewe uliuliza, "Ni nani huyu anayeficha mpango {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} bila maarifa?" \q Hakika nimenena mambo nisiyoyaelewa, \q mambo ya ajabu mno kwangu, ambayo sikuyajua.
sw.R: Uliuliza, "Ni nani huyu anayeficha mipango {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} kwa kusema bila kujua?" \q Ni kweli: nilisema juu ya mambo nisiyoyaelewa, \q mambo ya ajabu mno kwangu kuyajua.

vi.L: Ai [là] người này che giấu mưu định mà không có tri thức? \q Vì thế con đã nói, mà con không hiểu, \q [những điều] quá diệu kỳ đối với con, mà con không biết.
vi.B: Chúa đã hỏi: "Kẻ nào đây mà che giấu kế hoạch của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} bằng lời thiếu hiểu biết?" \q Quả thật con đã nói về điều con không hiểu, \q những điều quá diệu kỳ đối với con, mà con không biết.
vi.R: Chúa đã hỏi: "Kẻ nào đây mà nói năng thiếu hiểu biết, làm lu mờ kế hoạch của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}?" \q Đúng vậy, con đã nói về những điều con không hiểu, \q những điều quá kỳ diệu mà con không thể biết.

ko.L: 지식 없이 계획을 가리는 이 자는 누구냐? \q 그러므로 제가 말했으나 깨닫지 못했으니, \q 제게 너무 놀라워서 알지 못하던 [일들]이었습니다.
ko.B: 주님께서 "지식도 없이 내 계획을 가리는 이 자는 누구냐?" 하고 물으셨습니다. \q 참으로 저는 깨닫지도 못한 것을 말했습니다. \q 너무도 놀라워서 제가 알지 못하던 일들을 말했습니다.
ko.R: 주님께서 "알지도 못하면서 말하여 내 계획을 가리는 자가 누구냐?" 하고 물으셨습니다. \q 맞습니다. 저는 깨닫지 못한 일들을 말했습니다. \q 너무 놀라워서 제가 알 수 없는 일들을 말입니다.

pt.L: Quem [é] este que encobre o conselho sem conhecimento? \q Por isso falei, e não entendia, \q [coisas] maravilhosas demais para mim, que eu não conhecia.
pt.B: Tu perguntaste: "Quem é este que encobre o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} plano sem conhecimento?" \q De fato, falei do que eu não entendia, \q coisas maravilhosas demais para mim, que eu não conhecia.
pt.R: Tu perguntaste: "Quem é este que esconde os {{deity_pronoun:meus|Meus}} planos falando sem saber?" \q É verdade: falei de coisas que eu não entendia, \q coisas maravilhosas demais para eu saber.

decisions.choice: Job quotes the LORD's first question (38:2)
decisions.reason: These are almost exactly the words with which the LORD began (38:2), with "hides" in place of "darkens". Job repeats the question and answers it: the one who spoke without knowledge was himself.

decisions.choice: therefore: so it is true, I spoke
decisions.reason: The word usually means "therefore". Here it draws the conclusion from the question: since that is what was said of him, Job admits it.

decisions.choice: too wonderful for me: beyond what I can understand
decisions.reason: The word describes what is beyond human reach or understanding (Psalm 131:1; Psalm 139:6). Job does not say he was wicked; he says he spoke of things beyond his understanding.

decisions.choice: You asked, "..." (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew gives no sign that Job is quoting. Balanced and Readable supply "You asked" and quotation marks so the reader does not take the question for Job's own (m1). As in 38:2, "counsel" is rendered "plan", and the pronoun refers to God.

records.literal_gloss: Hear, please, and I will speak; I will ask you, and you make known to me.

en.L: Hear, please, and I will speak; \q I will ask you, and you make [it] known to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: You said, "Listen now, and I will speak; \q I will question you, and you will answer {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.R: You said, "Listen, and I will speak. \q I will ask you questions, and you must answer {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

es.L: Escucha ahora, y yo hablaré; \q yo te preguntaré, y tú {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} [lo] harás saber.
es.B: Tú dijiste: «Escucha ahora, y yo hablaré; \q yo te haré preguntas, y tú {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} responderás».
es.R: Tú dijiste: «Escucha, que yo voy a hablar. \q Yo te haré preguntas, y tú {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} tienes que responder».

fr.L: Écoute donc, et moi je parlerai ; \q je t’interrogerai, et toi, fais-le-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} savoir.
fr.B: Tu as dit : « Écoute maintenant, et je parlerai ; \q je vais t’interroger, et tu {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} répondras. »
fr.R: Tu as dit : « Écoute, je vais parler. \q Je vais te poser des questions, et tu devras {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} répondre. »

sw.L: Sikia, tafadhali, nami nitasema; \q nitakuuliza, nawe unijulishe [jibu].
sw.B: Ulisema, "Sikiliza sasa, nami nitasema; \q nitakuuliza maswali, nawe utanijibu."
sw.R: Ulisema, "Sikiliza, nami nitasema. \q Nitakuuliza maswali, nawe lazima unijibu."

vi.L: Hãy nghe, và chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ nói; \q Ta sẽ hỏi ngươi, và ngươi hãy cho {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} biết.
vi.B: Chúa đã phán: "Hãy nghe đây, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ nói; \q Ta sẽ chất vấn ngươi, và ngươi hãy trả lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."
vi.R: Chúa đã phán: "Hãy nghe, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ nói. \q Ta sẽ hỏi ngươi, và ngươi phải trả lời {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."

ko.L: 들어라, 내가 말하겠다. \q 내가 너에게 묻겠으니, 너는 나에게 알게 하여라.
ko.B: 주님께서 "이제 들어라, 내가 말하겠다. \q 내가 너에게 물을 테니 너는 내게 대답하여라" 하고 말씀하셨습니다.
ko.R: 주님께서 말씀하셨습니다. "들어라, 내가 말하겠다. \q 내가 묻겠다. 너는 내게 대답해야 한다."

pt.L: Ouve, por favor, e eu falarei; \q eu te perguntarei, e tu {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} farás saber.
pt.B: Tu disseste: "Ouve agora, e eu falarei; \q eu vou te interrogar, e tu {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} responderás."
pt.R: Tu disseste: "Escuta, e eu vou falar. \q Eu vou te fazer perguntas, e tu tens de {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} responder."

decisions.choice: Job quotes the LORD's challenge (38:3; 40:7)
decisions.reason: The second line repeats the LORD's words in 38:3 and 40:7 exactly: "I will ask you, and you make it known to me." So the verse is best read as a second quotation, like 42:3. Some read it as Job asking God to listen to him, but the words are the LORD's.

decisions.choice: hear, and I will speak: the reverse of what Job once demanded
decisions.reason: Job had challenged God: "Call, and I will answer, or let me speak, and you reply" (13:22). In the storm it was God who called and Job who had to answer.

decisions.choice: You said, "..." (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 42:3, Balanced and Readable mark the quotation (m1). In the quoted words "I" is the LORD and "you" is Job.

decisions.choice: "Ta" and "ngươi" inside the quotation
decisions.reason: In the quoted words God is the speaker (m1), so they keep God's own pronouns from 40:7.

decisions.choice: the quoted words keep God's 해라체 (너, 나), inside Job's 합쇼체
decisions.reason: Job repeats God's own challenge (m1), so the quoted words keep the level God used in 38:3 and 40:7.

decisions.choice: eu te perguntarei, e tu me farás saber (L); eu vou te interrogar (B)
alternatives: eu te perguntarei, e tu me responderás (L)
decisions.reason: Job quotes the LORD's challenge of 38:3 and 40:7 (m1), so Literal repeats the Portuguese of those verses word for word, and Balanced keeps their "eu vou te interrogar". Inside the quotation the LORD speaks, so "te" is Job and the "me" that refers to God has the deity_pronoun span.

records.literal_gloss: By hearing of ear I had heard of you, and now eye my has seen you.

en.L: By the hearing of the ear I had heard of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, \q but now my eye has seen {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.B: I had heard of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} by what my ears were told, \q but now my own eyes have seen {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.R: Before, I had only heard about {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. \q But now I have seen {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} with my own eyes.

es.L: Con el oír del oído había oído de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, \q pero ahora mi ojo {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} ha visto.
es.B: Había oído hablar de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} por lo que otros me contaban, \q pero ahora {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} han visto mis ojos.
es.R: Antes solo sabía de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} por lo que había oído. \q Pero ahora {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} he visto yo mismo, con mis ojos.

fr.L: Par ce qu’entend l’oreille, j’avais entendu parler de {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}, \q mais à présent mon œil {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}a vu.
fr.B: J’avais entendu parler de {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} par ce qu’on m’en disait, \q mais à présent ce sont mes propres yeux qui {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}ont vu.
fr.R: Avant, je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} connaissais seulement par ce que j’avais entendu. \q Mais à présent, je {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}ai vu de mes yeux.

sw.L: Kwa habari ya sikio nilikuwa nimesikia juu {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}, \q lakini sasa jicho langu limekuona.
sw.B: Nilikuwa nimesikia habari {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}} kwa yale niliyoambiwa, \q lakini sasa macho yangu mwenyewe yamekuona.
sw.R: Zamani nilisikia tu habari {{deity_pronoun:zako|Zako}}. \q Lakini sasa nimekuona kwa macho yangu mwenyewe.

vi.L: Bằng cái nghe của tai, con đã nghe về Chúa, \q nhưng nay mắt con đã thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Con đã biết về Chúa qua những điều tai con được nghe kể, \q nhưng giờ đây chính mắt con đã thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Trước kia con chỉ nghe nói về Chúa. \q Nhưng giờ đây con đã tận mắt thấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 귀에 들리는 소문으로 제가 주님에 대해 들었으나, \q 이제는 제 눈이 주님을 뵈었습니다.
ko.B: 제 귀에 전해진 말로 주님에 관해 들었지만, \q 이제는 바로 제 눈이 주님을 뵈었습니다.
ko.R: 전에는 다른 사람에게서 주님 이야기를 들었을 뿐입니다. \q 그러나 이제는 제가 주님을 직접 뵈었습니다.

pt.L: Pelo ouvir do ouvido eu tinha ouvido falar de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}, \q mas agora o meu olho {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} viu.
pt.B: Eu tinha ouvido falar de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}} pelo que os meus ouvidos escutaram, \q mas agora os meus próprios olhos {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} viram.
pt.R: Antes, eu só tinha ouvido falar de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}. \q Mas agora eu {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} vi com os meus próprios olhos.

decisions.choice: by the hearing of the ear: by report, what others say
decisions.reason: To know by the hearing of the ear is to know secondhand, by what one has been told (28:22; Psalm 18:45). Job's knowledge of God had been real, but at a distance.

decisions.choice: now my eye has seen you: Job has met God himself
decisions.reason: Job had longed to see God (19:26-27). In the storm God has come and spoken to him. The text does not describe what Job saw; the point is that he has met God directly and not only heard about him.

decisions.choice: Before, I had only heard (R)
decisions.reason: Readable adds "before" and "only" to bring out the contrast between hearing and seeing (m1).

decisions.choice: "Con el oír del oído" (L), "por lo que otros me contaban" (B)
decisions.reason: Drafted fresh from the Hebrew: "the hearing of the ear" means knowledge by report (m1). The familiar "de oídas te había oído" of older versions is avoided.

decisions.choice: "뵈었습니다" for seeing God
decisions.reason: Korean uses the humble verb 뵙다 for seeing one far above oneself; Job's words to God are in 합쇼체 throughout.

records.literal_gloss: Therefore I reject and I repent on dust and ashes.

en.L: Therefore I retract [my words], \q and I repent in dust and ashes.
en.B: So I take back what I said, \q and I repent in dust and ashes.

pt.L: Por isso eu me retrato \q e me arrependo no pó e na cinza.

decisions.choice: I reject: I retract what I said
decisions.reason: The verb means to reject or despise, but here it has no object, and what Job rejects must be supplied. Most likely it is his own words, spoken without knowledge (42:3; compare 40:4-5). Others supply "myself", or take it as in 7:16, "I loathe my life".

decisions.choice: I repent: I turn from my former position
alternatives: I am comforted concerning dust and ashes
decisions.reason: The verb can mean to be sorry and change one's mind, or to be comforted (2:11 uses it of the friends coming to comfort Job). With "concerning" it can mean "I relent concerning" or "I am comforted about dust and ashes", that is, Job accepts his place as a mortal man. Repentance is followed here, but the line is not certain.

decisions.choice: dust and ashes: the sign of mourning and of human lowliness
decisions.reason: Job had sat among the ashes (2:8), and his friends threw dust on their heads (2:12). Dust and ashes also stand for what a human being is before God (30:19; Genesis 18:27).

decisions.choice: what Job repents of: not the sins the friends charged him with
decisions.reason: The LORD says next that Job has spoken what is right about him, and the friends have not (42:7-8). Job does not confess the hidden wickedness the friends claimed caused his suffering; he takes back his demand that God answer to him, spoken without knowledge (42:3).

decisions.choice: [my words] (L); what I said (B, R)
decisions.reason: English needs an object for the verb. Every level supplies "my words" or "what I said" following m1; Literal brackets it.

decisions.choice: "retiro [mis palabras] ... me arrepiento"
alternatives: "me aborrezco"; "me consuelo en cuanto al polvo y la ceniza"
decisions.reason: Follows m1 and m2: Job takes back his words and repents; the other readings stay in the meaning decisions.

decisions.choice: "je retire [mes paroles] ... je me repens"
alternatives: "je me méprise"; "je me console sur la poussière et la cendre"
decisions.reason: Follows m1 and m2; the familiar "je me condamne" is avoided because it supplies "myself", which m1 does not prefer.

decisions.choice: "ninayafuta [maneno yangu] ... natubu"
decisions.reason: Follows m1 and m2: Job retracts his words and repents; "najichukia" (I despise myself) supplies an object the meaning decision does not prefer.

decisions.choice: "rút lại [lời mình] ... ăn năn"
decisions.reason: Follows m1 and m2: Job takes back what he said and repents; the alternatives are in the meaning decisions.

decisions.choice: "[제 말을] 물리고 ... 회개합니다"
decisions.reason: Follows m1 and m2: Job takes back his words and repents; 물리다 and 취소하다 say "take back" in plain Korean.

decisions.choice: eu me retrato (L, B), volto atrás no que eu disse (R); me arrependo no pó e na cinza
decisions.reason: The first verb has no object, and the meaning notes read it as Job withdrawing his words (m1, m4), not despising himself: Portuguese "retratar-se" says exactly that, so Literal needs no bracketed object, and Balanced adds "do que disse" as the English adds "what I said". "Arrepender-se" is turning from a former position (m2). "Pó e cinza" keeps the words of 30:19 and Genesis 18:27 (m3), with the articles Portuguese uses after "no".

pt.L: E aconteceu que, depois que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} falou estas palavras a Jó, {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} disse a Elifaz, o temanita: "A {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} ira se acendeu contra ti e contra os teus dois amigos, porque vocês não falaram de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} [o que é] certo, como o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} escravo Jó [falou].
pt.B: Depois que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} falou essas palavras a Jó, {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} disse a Elifaz, o temanita: "A {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} ira está acesa contra ti e contra os teus dois amigos, porque vocês não falaram a {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} respeito o que é certo, como falou o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} servo Jó.
pt.R: Depois que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} terminou de falar com Jó, {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} disse a Elifaz, o temanita: "Estou irado contigo e com os teus dois amigos. Vocês não disseram o que é certo a {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} respeito, como disse o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} servo Jó.

decisions.choice: the story returns to prose, and the LORD speaks to the friends
decisions.reason: With these words the book returns to the prose of chapters 1-2 and to the divine name used there. The LORD has finished speaking to Job (38:1-41:26) and now turns to Eliphaz, the first and probably the oldest of the friends (4:1; 15:10).

decisions.choice: what is right: what is true and well founded
decisions.reason: The word means firm, established, reliable (Psalm 5:10, "nothing reliable in their mouth"). The friends' speeches about God were not true to him; Job's were.

decisions.choice: of me: about God
decisions.reason: The preposition usually means "to", but it can also mean "about". The friends spoke about God rather than to him, while Job spoke to God as well as about him. "About me" fits both the friends and Job, and is followed; "to me" would point to Job's prayers and complaints addressed to God.

decisions.choice: Job, not the friends, spoke rightly
decisions.reason: The friends had defended God by insisting that Job must be guilty; Job had warned them that God would rebuke them for speaking falsely on his behalf (13:7-10). The LORD calls Job "my servant" as in the prologue (1:8; 2:3). He has rebuked Job's words spoken without knowledge (38:2; 40:2, 8), but he does not count Job among those who spoke wrongly of him.

decisions.choice: slave (L), servant (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:8, Literal says "slave" and Balanced and Readable "servant" for the word that means one who belongs to his master; here it is a title of honor.

decisions.choice: I am angry with you (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the picture of burning anger means.

decisions.choice: plural_you on every plural "you" in God's words to the three friends (42:7-8)
decisions.reason: The LORD speaks to Eliphaz ("you", "your two friends") and then to all three ("you have not spoken"); Spanish shows the plural in the verb, under the setting.

decisions.choice: God says "ngươi" to Eliphaz and "các ngươi" to the three, "Ta" for himself
decisions.reason: As God's words to the Accuser in 1-2 and to Job in 38-41.

decisions.choice: God speaks to Eliphaz and the friends in 해라체 with 너, 너희, naming Job "내 종 욥" at every level
decisions.reason: As God speaks to the Accuser (1:8) and to Job (38-41); 종 at every level as in 1:8.

decisions.choice: "tu" to Eliphaz ("contra ti", "os teus dois amigos"); "vocês" to the three ("vocês não falaram")
decisions.reason: God speaks to one person with "tu" (docs/pentateuch-portuguese-terms.md; JOB_NOTE), so Eliphaz is "tu"; the verb "you have spoken" is plural in the Hebrew, addressed to all three friends, and God speaks to a group with "vocês", as also in verse 8.

records.literal_gloss: And now take for yourselves seven bulls and seven rams and go to my slave Job, and offer up a burnt offering for yourselves, and Job my slave will pray for you; for his face I will lift up, so as not to do with you folly, for not you have spoken of me [what is] right like my slave Job.

en.L: And now take for yourselves seven bulls and seven rams, and go to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} slave Job and offer up a burnt offering for yourselves, and Job {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} slave will pray for you; for his face I will lift up, so that I do not deal with you [according to your] folly; for you have not spoken of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} [what is] right, as {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} slave Job [has]."
en.B: So now take seven bulls and seven rams, go to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant Job, and offer a burnt offering for yourselves. My servant Job will pray for you, and I will accept his prayer and not deal with you as your folly deserves. For you have not spoken of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} what is right, as {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant Job has."
en.R: Now take seven bulls and seven rams. Go to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant Job and offer them as a burnt offering for yourselves. My servant Job will pray for you, and I will accept his prayer. Then I will not punish you for your foolishness. You have not said what is right about {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, as {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant Job has."

es.L: Y ahora, {{plural_you:tomen|tomad}} para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} siete toros y siete carneros, y {{plural_you:vayan|id}} a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} esclavo Job, y {{plural_you:ofrezcan|ofreced}} holocausto por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y Job, {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} esclavo, orará por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}; porque su rostro alzaré, para no hacer con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} [según {{plural_you:su|vuestra}}] insensatez; porque no {{plural_you:han hablado|habéis hablado}} de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} [lo que es] recto, como {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} esclavo Job».
es.B: Ahora, pues, {{plural_you:tomen|tomad}} siete toros y siete carneros, {{plural_you:vayan|id}} a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo Job y {{plural_you:ofrezcan|ofreced}} un holocausto por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Mi siervo Job orará por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y yo aceptaré su oración y no {{plural_you:los|os}} trataré como {{plural_you:merece su insensatez|merece vuestra insensatez}}. Porque no {{plural_you:han hablado|habéis hablado}} de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} lo que es recto, como lo ha hecho {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo Job».
es.R: Ahora {{plural_you:tomen|tomad}} siete toros y siete carneros. {{plural_you:Vayan|Id}} a ver a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo Job y {{plural_you:ofrézcanlos|ofrecedlos}} como holocausto por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Mi siervo Job orará por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y yo aceptaré su oración. Así no {{plural_you:los|os}} castigaré por {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} necedad. No {{plural_you:han dicho|habéis dicho}} lo que es correcto acerca de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, como lo ha hecho {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} siervo Job».

fr.L: Et maintenant, prenez pour vous sept taureaux et sept béliers, et allez vers {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} esclave Job, et offrez un holocauste pour vous, et Job, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} esclave, priera pour vous ; car je relèverai sa face, pour ne pas agir envers vous [selon votre] folie ; car vous n’avez pas dit de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} [ce qui est] juste, comme {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} esclave Job. »
fr.B: Maintenant donc, prenez sept taureaux et sept béliers, allez trouver {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} serviteur Job et offrez un holocauste pour vous. Mon serviteur Job priera pour vous, et j’accueillerai sa prière, pour ne pas vous traiter comme le mériterait votre folie. Car vous n’avez pas parlé de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} avec justesse, comme l’a fait {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} serviteur Job. »
fr.R: Maintenant, prenez sept taureaux et sept béliers. Allez trouver {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} serviteur Job et offrez-les en holocauste pour vous. Mon serviteur Job priera pour vous, et j’accepterai sa prière. Alors je ne vous punirai pas pour votre folie. Vous n’avez pas dit ce qui est juste à {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} sujet, comme l’a fait {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} serviteur Job. »

sw.L: Basi sasa, jitwalieni ng'ombe dume saba na kondoo dume saba, mwende kwa mtumwa {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} Ayubu, mkajitolee sadaka ya kuteketezwa; na Ayubu mtumwa {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} atawaombea; kwa maana nitauinua uso wake, nisiwatendee [kwa kadiri ya] upumbavu [wenu]; kwa maana hamkusema juu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} [yaliyo] sawa, kama mtumwa {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} Ayubu [alivyosema]."
sw.B: Basi sasa chukueni ng'ombe dume saba na kondoo dume saba, mwende kwa mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} Ayubu, mkatoe sadaka ya kuteketezwa kwa ajili yenu. Mtumishi wangu Ayubu atawaombea, nami nitapokea maombi yake na sitawatendea kama upumbavu wenu unavyostahili. Kwa maana hamkusema yaliyo sawa juu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, kama alivyosema mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} Ayubu."
sw.R: Sasa chukueni ng'ombe dume saba na kondoo dume saba. Nendeni kwa mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} Ayubu, mkawatoe sadaka ya kuteketezwa kwa ajili yenu. Mtumishi wangu Ayubu atawaombea, nami nitapokea maombi yake. Kisha sitawaadhibu kwa sababu ya upumbavu wenu. Hamkusema yaliyo sawa juu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, kama alivyosema mtumishi {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} Ayubu."

vi.L: Vậy bây giờ, các ngươi hãy lấy cho mình bảy con bò đực và bảy con chiên đực, rồi đi đến cùng nô lệ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là Gióp, và dâng tế lễ thiêu cho mình; rồi Gióp, nô lệ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, sẽ cầu nguyện cho các ngươi; vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ nâng mặt người lên, để {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không xử với các ngươi [theo] sự ngu dại [của các ngươi]; vì các ngươi đã không nói về {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} [điều] đúng đắn như nô lệ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là Gióp [đã nói]."
vi.B: Vậy bây giờ, các ngươi hãy lấy bảy con bò đực và bảy con chiên đực, đi đến cùng đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là Gióp và dâng tế lễ thiêu cho mình. Đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là Gióp sẽ cầu nguyện cho các ngươi, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ nhậm lời người, không xử với các ngươi theo sự ngu dại các ngươi đáng chịu. Vì các ngươi đã không nói về {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} điều đúng đắn như đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là Gióp đã nói."
vi.R: Bây giờ các ngươi hãy lấy bảy con bò đực và bảy con chiên đực. Hãy đến gặp đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là Gióp và dâng chúng làm tế lễ thiêu cho mình. Đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là Gióp sẽ cầu nguyện cho các ngươi, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ nhậm lời người. Như thế {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không phạt các ngươi vì sự ngu dại của các ngươi. Các ngươi đã không nói điều đúng về {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} như đầy tớ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là Gióp đã nói."

ko.L: 그러므로 이제 너희는 너희를 위하여 수소 일곱 마리와 숫양 일곱 마리를 가지고 내 종 욥에게 가서, 너희를 위하여 번제를 드려라. 그러면 내 종 욥이 너희를 위하여 기도할 것이다. 내가 그의 얼굴을 들어 주어, 너희에게 [너희의] 어리석음대로 행하지 않을 것이다. 너희가 나에 대하여 내 종 욥처럼 옳은 [것을] 말하지 않았기 때문이다."
ko.B: 이제 너희는 수소 일곱 마리와 숫양 일곱 마리를 가지고 내 종 욥에게 가서 너희를 위하여 번제를 드려라. 내 종 욥이 너희를 위하여 기도할 것이고, 나는 그의 기도를 받아들여 너희의 어리석음에 마땅한 대로 너희를 대하지 않겠다. 너희는 내 종 욥처럼 나에 대해 옳은 것을 말하지 않았다."
ko.R: 이제 수소 일곱 마리와 숫양 일곱 마리를 가지고 내 종 욥에게 가서 너희를 위해 번제로 바쳐라. 내 종 욥이 너희를 위해 기도할 것이고, 나는 그의 기도를 들어줄 것이다. 그러면 너희가 어리석게 군 것을 벌하지 않겠다. 너희는 내 종 욥처럼 나에 대해 옳은 말을 하지 않았다."

pt.L: E agora tomem para vocês sete touros e sete carneiros, e vão ao {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} escravo Jó, e ofereçam um holocausto por vocês, e Jó, o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} escravo, orará por vocês; porque o rosto dele eu levantarei, para que eu não trate vocês [segundo a sua] insensatez; porque vocês não falaram de {{deity_pronoun:mim|Mim}} [o que é] certo, como o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} escravo Jó [falou]."
pt.B: Agora, peguem sete touros e sete carneiros, vão até o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} servo Jó e ofereçam um holocausto por vocês. O {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} servo Jó orará por vocês, e eu aceitarei a oração dele e não tratarei vocês como a insensatez de vocês merece. Pois vocês não falaram a {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} respeito o que é certo, como falou o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} servo Jó."
pt.R: Agora peguem sete touros e sete carneiros. Vão até o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} servo Jó e ofereçam os animais como holocausto por vocês. O {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} servo Jó vai orar por vocês, e eu vou aceitar a oração dele. Então não vou castigar vocês pela insensatez de vocês. Vocês não disseram o que é certo a {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} respeito, como disse o {{deity_pronoun:meu|Meu}} servo Jó."

decisions.choice: seven bulls and seven rams as a burnt offering: a large and complete sacrifice
decisions.reason: Seven of each makes a full and costly offering (Numbers 23:1; 1 Chronicles 15:26). The burnt offering was wholly burned on the altar. Job had offered burnt offerings for his children in case they had sinned (1:5); now he stands between God and his friends.

decisions.choice: I will lift up his face: I will accept him and his prayer
decisions.reason: To lift up someone's face is to receive them with favor and grant their request (Genesis 19:21; 1 Samuel 25:35). God will hear Job's prayer for the friends who wronged him.

decisions.choice: not to deal with you according to your folly
alternatives: so as not to disgrace you
decisions.reason: The noun means senseless or shameful folly, the outrage a fool commits (Genesis 34:7; 1 Samuel 25:25). It can mean either the friends' folly, which God will not repay, or a disgrace God would bring on them; both mean that God will spare them because of Job's prayer.

decisions.choice: Job prays for the friends
decisions.reason: Job, whom the friends condemned, becomes the one through whose prayer they are forgiven, as Abraham and Moses prayed for others (Genesis 20:7, 17; Numbers 21:7).

decisions.choice: I will accept his prayer (B, R)
alternatives: I will lift up his face
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the meaning of the idiom (m2) and name the prayer it refers to.

decisions.choice: slave (L), servant (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 42:7 and 1:8.

decisions.choice: o meu escravo Jó (L); o meu servo Jó (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:8 and 2:3, where God first calls Job his servant: Literal "escravo", Balanced and Readable "servo" (docs/pentateuch-portuguese-terms.md), so the frame of the book closes with the words it opened with.

source.text: וַיֵּלְכוּ֩ אֱלִיפַ֨ז הַתֵּֽימָנִ֜י וּבִלְדַּ֣ד הַשּׁוּחִ֗י צֹפַר֙ הַנַּ֣עֲמָתִ֔י וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֔וּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר דִּבֶּ֥ר אֲלֵיהֶ֖ם יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּשָּׂ֥א יְהוָ֖ה אֶת־פְּנֵ֥י אִיּֽוֹב׃

records.literal_gloss: And went Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite, Zophar the Naamathite, and did as had spoken to them the LORD; and lifted up the LORD [the] face of Job.

en.L: And Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite [and] Zophar the Naamathite went and did as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had spoken to them; and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lifted up the face of Job.
en.B: So Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went and did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told them, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} accepted Job's prayer.
en.R: So Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went and did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told them. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} accepted Job's prayer.

es.L: Y fueron Elifaz el temanita y Bildad el suhita [y] Zofar el naamatita, e hicieron como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} les había dicho; y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} alzó el rostro de Job.
es.B: Entonces Elifaz el temanita, Bildad el suhita y Zofar el naamatita fueron e hicieron lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} les había mandado, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} aceptó la oración de Job.
es.R: Así que Elifaz el temanita, Bildad el suhita y Zofar el naamatita fueron e hicieron lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} les había dicho. Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} aceptó la oración de Job.

fr.L: Et Éliphaz le Témanite et Bildad le Shouhite [et] Tsophar le Naamatite allèrent et firent comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} leur avait dit ; et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} releva la face de Job.
fr.B: Éliphaz le Témanite, Bildad le Shouhite et Tsophar le Naamatite allèrent donc faire ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} leur avait dit, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} accueillit la prière de Job.
fr.R: Alors Éliphaz le Témanite, Bildad le Shouhite et Tsophar le Naamatite sont allés faire ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} leur avait dit. Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a accepté la prière de Job.

sw.L: Basi Elifazi Mtemani na Bildadi Mshua [na] Sofari Mnaamathi wakaenda, wakafanya kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyowaambia; na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akauinua uso wa Ayubu.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo Elifazi Mtemani, Bildadi Mshua na Sofari Mnaamathi walikwenda, wakafanya kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyowaagiza, naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akayapokea maombi ya Ayubu.
sw.R: Basi Elifazi Mtemani, Bildadi Mshua na Sofari Mnaamathi walikwenda, wakafanya kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyowaambia. Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akayapokea maombi ya Ayubu.

vi.L: Vậy Ê-li-pha người Thê-man và Binh-đát người Su-ách [và] Sô-pha người Na-a-ma đi và làm như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phán với họ; và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} nâng mặt Gióp lên.
vi.B: Vậy Ê-li-pha người Thê-man, Binh-đát người Su-ách và Sô-pha người Na-a-ma đi làm theo điều {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phán dặn họ, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} nhậm lời cầu nguyện của Gióp.
vi.R: Vậy Ê-li-pha người Thê-man, Binh-đát người Su-ách và Sô-pha người Na-a-ma đi làm đúng như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã bảo họ. Và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} nhậm lời cầu nguyện của Gióp.

ko.L: 그래서 데만 사람 엘리바스와 수아 사람 빌닷[과] 나아마 사람 소발이 가서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그들에게 말씀하신 대로 행하였다. 그리고 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 욥의 얼굴을 들어 주셨다.
ko.B: 그래서 데만 사람 엘리바스와 수아 사람 빌닷과 나아마 사람 소발이 가서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그들에게 이르신 대로 하였고, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 욥의 기도를 받아들이셨다.
ko.R: 그래서 데만 사람 엘리바스와 수아 사람 빌닷과 나아마 사람 소발은 가서 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 말씀하신 대로 했다. 그러자 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 욥의 기도를 들어주셨다.

pt.L: E Elifaz, o temanita, e Bildade, o suíta, [e] Zofar, o naamatita, foram e fizeram como {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} lhes tinha falado; e {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} levantou o rosto de Jó.
pt.B: Então Elifaz, o temanita, Bildade, o suíta, e Zofar, o naamatita, foram e fizeram o que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} lhes tinha ordenado, e {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} aceitou a oração de Jó.
pt.R: Então Elifaz, o temanita, Bildade, o suíta, e Zofar, o naamatita, foram e fizeram o que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} lhes tinha mandado. E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} aceitou a oração de Jó.

decisions.choice: the LORD lifted up the face of Job: he accepted Job and his prayer
decisions.reason: The same idiom as in 42:8: God received Job with favor and granted his prayer for his friends. The friends are named in full for the last time, as when they came (2:11).

decisions.choice: accepted Job's prayer (B, R)
alternatives: lifted up the face of Job
decisions.reason: As in 42:8, Balanced and Readable give the meaning of the idiom and name the prayer.

source.text: וַֽיהוָ֗ה שָׁ֚ב אֶת־שְׁב֣וּת אִיּ֔וֹב בְּהִֽתְפַּֽלְל֖וֹ בְּעַ֣ד רֵעֵ֑הוּ וַ֧יֹּסֶף יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְאִיּ֖וֹב לְמִשְׁנֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And the LORD turned back the captivity of Job when he prayed for his friends, and increased the LORD all that [belonged] to Job to double.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} turned back the captivity of Job when he prayed for his friends, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} increased all that Job had to double.
en.B: When Job prayed for his friends, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} restored his fortunes, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Job twice as much as he had before.
en.R: When Job prayed for his friends, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} made him prosperous again. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} gave him twice as much as he had before.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} hizo volver la cautividad de Job cuando él oró por sus amigos, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} aumentó al doble todo lo que Job tenía.
es.B: Cuando Job oró por sus amigos, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} restauró su suerte, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dio a Job el doble de lo que antes tenía.
es.R: Cuando Job oró por sus amigos, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} lo hizo prosperar de nuevo. {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dio el doble de lo que tenía antes.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ramena la captivité de Job, quand il pria pour ses amis, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} augmenta du double tout ce qu’avait Job.
fr.B: Quand Job pria pour ses amis, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} rétablit son sort, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui donna le double de tout ce qu’il avait possédé.
fr.R: Quand Job a prié pour ses amis, {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’a rendu prospère de nouveau. {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui a donné deux fois plus qu’il n’avait avant.

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaugeuza utumwa wa Ayubu alipowaombea rafiki zake, na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaongeza vyote alivyokuwa navyo Ayubu mara mbili.
sw.B: Ayubu alipowaombea rafiki zake, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alirudisha hali yake, na {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akampa Ayubu mara mbili ya vyote alivyokuwa navyo kwanza.
sw.R: Ayubu alipowaombea rafiki zake, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimfanikisha tena. {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimpa mara mbili ya vile alivyokuwa navyo zamani.

vi.L: Và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} xoay chuyển cảnh lưu đày của Gióp khi ông cầu nguyện cho các bạn mình, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} gia tăng gấp đôi mọi điều Gióp có.
vi.B: Khi Gióp cầu nguyện cho các bạn mình, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phục hồi cơ nghiệp cho ông, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ban cho Gióp gấp đôi những gì ông có trước kia.
vi.R: Khi Gióp cầu nguyện cho các bạn mình, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} cho ông được thịnh vượng trở lại. {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ban cho ông gấp đôi những gì ông có trước đây.

ko.L: 욥이 자기 친구들을 위하여 기도할 때에 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 욥의 포로 된 것을 돌이키셨고, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 욥이 가졌던 모든 것을 갑절로 더하셨다.
ko.B: 욥이 친구들을 위하여 기도하자 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그의 형편을 회복시키셨고, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 욥에게 전에 가졌던 것보다 갑절을 주셨다.
ko.R: 욥이 친구들을 위해 기도하자 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그를 다시 잘살게 해 주셨다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 그가 전에 가졌던 것의 두 배를 주셨다.

pt.L: E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} fez voltar o cativeiro de Jó quando ele orou pelos seus amigos, e {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} aumentou em dobro tudo o que Jó tinha.
pt.B: Quando Jó orou pelos seus amigos, {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} restaurou a sua sorte, e {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} deu a Jó o dobro de tudo o que ele tinha antes.
pt.R: Quando Jó orou pelos seus amigos, {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} o fez prosperar de novo. {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} lhe deu o dobro do que ele tinha antes.

decisions.choice: turned back the captivity: restored his fortunes
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of God bringing his people back from exile (Deuteronomy 30:3; Psalm 126:4) and more generally of restoring what was lost. Job was never a captive; the LORD turned his ruin back into prosperity. The written text and the scribes' reading note spell the noun slightly differently; the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: when he prayed for his friends
decisions.reason: The restoration comes as Job prays for the men who had wronged him (42:8). The text links the two without saying that the one caused the other.

decisions.choice: to double: twice as much
decisions.reason: The numbers in 42:12 are exactly twice those of 1:3. Double repayment is what the law requires of a thief (Exodus 22:3, 6, 8, numbered 22:4, 7, 9 in many Bibles), so Job's losses are more than made good.

decisions.choice: restored his fortunes (B); made him prosperous again (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the meaning of the phrase (m1); Literal keeps the picture.

decisions.choice: em dobro (L); o dobro (B, R)
decisions.reason: "O dobro" is the plain Portuguese for twice as much, the double that m3 links to the numbers of 42:12 and 1:3; Literal keeps the Hebrew "increased ... to double" as "aumentou em dobro".

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ אֵ֠לָיו כָּל־אֶחָ֨יו וְכָל־אַחְיוֹתָ֜יו וְכָל־יֹדְעָ֣יו לְפָנִ֗ים וַיֹּאכְל֨וּ עִמּ֣וֹ לֶחֶם֮ בְּבֵיתוֹ֒ וַיָּנֻ֤דוּ לוֹ֙ וַיְנַחֲמ֣וּ אֹת֔וֹ עַ֚ל כָּל־הָ֣רָעָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־הֵבִ֥יא יְהוָ֖ה עָלָ֑יו וַיִּתְּנוּ־ל֗וֹ אִ֚ישׁ קְשִׂיטָ֣ה אֶחָ֔ת וְאִ֕ישׁ נֶ֥זֶם זָהָ֖ב אֶחָֽד׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And came to him all his brothers and all his sisters and all [who] knew him before, and they ate with him bread in his house; and they showed sympathy to him and comforted him over all the evil that had brought the LORD on him; and gave to him each one qesitah one and each one ring of gold one.

en.L: And there came to him all his brothers and all his sisters and all who had known him before, and they ate bread with him in his house; and they showed him sympathy and comforted him over all the evil that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had brought upon him; and each gave him one qesitah and each one ring of gold.
en.B: All his brothers and sisters and everyone who had known him before came and ate a meal with him in his house. They showed him sympathy and comforted him for all the trouble {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had brought on him, and each of them gave him {{units:a piece of money|a qesitah}} and a gold ring.
en.R: All his brothers and sisters and all his old friends came to his house and ate with him. They showed that they cared, and they comforted him for all the trouble {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had brought on him. Each of them gave him {{units:a piece of money|a qesitah}} and a gold ring.

es.L: Y vinieron a él todos sus hermanos y todas sus hermanas y todos los que lo habían conocido antes, y comieron pan con él en su casa; y le mostraron compasión y lo consolaron por todo el mal que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había traído sobre él; y cada uno le dio una quesitá, y cada uno un anillo de oro.
es.B: Todos sus hermanos y hermanas y todos los que lo habían conocido antes vinieron y comieron con él en su casa. Le mostraron su compasión y lo consolaron por todas las desgracias que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había traído sobre él, y cada uno le dio {{units:una moneda|una quesitá}} y un anillo de oro.
es.R: Todos sus hermanos y hermanas y todos sus viejos amigos vinieron a su casa y comieron con él. Le mostraron su cariño y lo consolaron por todas las desgracias que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había traído sobre él. Cada uno le regaló {{units:una moneda|una quesitá}} y un anillo de oro.

fr.L: Et vinrent vers lui tous ses frères et toutes ses sœurs et tous ceux qui l’avaient connu auparavant, et ils mangèrent du pain avec lui dans sa maison ; et ils lui témoignèrent leur compassion et le consolèrent de tout le mal que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avait fait venir sur lui ; et chacun lui donna une qesita, et chacun un anneau d’or.
fr.B: Tous ses frères et toutes ses sœurs, et tous ceux qui l’avaient connu auparavant, vinrent manger avec lui dans sa maison. Ils lui témoignèrent leur compassion et le consolèrent de tous les malheurs que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avait fait venir sur lui, et chacun lui donna {{units:une pièce d’argent|une qesita}} et un anneau d’or.
fr.R: Tous ses frères et ses sœurs et tous ses anciens amis sont venus chez lui et ont mangé avec lui. Ils lui ont montré qu’ils l’aimaient et l’ont consolé de tous les malheurs que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avait fait venir sur lui. Chacun lui a donné {{units:une pièce d’argent|une qesita}} et un anneau d’or.

sw.L: Wakaja kwake ndugu zake wote wa kiume na dada zake wote na wote waliomjua zamani, wakala mkate pamoja naye nyumbani mwake; wakamhurumia na kumfariji juu ya mabaya yote ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa ameleta juu yake; na kila mmoja akampa kesita moja, na kila mmoja pete moja ya dhahabu.
sw.B: Ndugu zake wote wa kiume na wa kike, na wote waliomjua zamani, walikuja wakala chakula pamoja naye nyumbani mwake. Walimhurumia na kumfariji kwa ajili ya taabu zote ambazo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa ameleta juu yake, na kila mmoja akampa {{units:kipande cha fedha|kesita moja}} na pete ya dhahabu.
sw.R: Ndugu zake wote wa kiume na wa kike na rafiki zake wote wa zamani walikuja nyumbani kwake wakala pamoja naye. Walimwonyesha kwamba wanamjali, wakamfariji kwa ajili ya mabaya yote ambayo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alikuwa ameleta juu yake. Kila mmoja wao akampa {{units:kipande cha fedha|kesita moja}} na pete ya dhahabu.

vi.L: Và hết thảy anh em trai, hết thảy chị em gái của ông, cùng hết thảy những người quen biết ông trước kia đều đến cùng ông, và ăn bánh với ông trong nhà ông; họ chia buồn và an ủi ông về mọi điều dữ mà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã giáng trên ông; và mỗi người tặng ông một kê-si-ta, và mỗi người một chiếc nhẫn vàng.
vi.B: Tất cả anh em, chị em của ông và mọi người quen biết ông trước kia đều đến ăn uống với ông trong nhà ông. Họ chia buồn và an ủi ông về mọi tai họa mà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã giáng trên ông, và mỗi người tặng ông {{units:một miếng bạc|một kê-si-ta}} và một chiếc nhẫn vàng.
vi.R: Tất cả anh chị em của ông và mọi bạn bè cũ đều đến nhà ăn uống với ông. Họ tỏ lòng quan tâm và an ủi ông về mọi tai họa mà {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã giáng trên ông. Mỗi người tặng ông {{units:một miếng bạc|một kê-si-ta}} và một chiếc nhẫn vàng.

ko.L: 그의 모든 형제와 모든 자매와 전에 그를 알던 모든 사람이 그에게 와서, 그의 집에서 그와 함께 빵을 먹었다. 그들은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그에게 내리신 모든 재앙에 대하여 그와 함께 슬퍼하고 그를 위로하였다. 그리고 각 사람이 크시타 하나씩과 금고리 하나씩을 그에게 주었다.
ko.B: 그의 형제자매들과 전에 그를 알던 모든 사람이 와서 그의 집에서 그와 함께 음식을 먹었다. 그들은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그에게 내리신 모든 재앙을 두고 그와 함께 슬퍼하며 그를 위로하였고, 저마다 그에게 {{units:돈 한 닢|크시타 하나}}씩과 금고리 하나씩을 주었다.
ko.R: 그의 형제자매들과 옛 친구들이 모두 그의 집에 와서 함께 음식을 먹었다. 그들은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 그에게 내리신 모든 고난을 두고 그를 아끼는 마음을 보이며 위로해 주었다. 저마다 그에게 {{units:돈 한 닢|크시타 하나}}씩과 금반지 하나씩을 주었다.

pt.L: E vieram a ele todos os seus irmãos e todas as suas irmãs e todos os que o tinham conhecido antes, e comeram pão com ele na sua casa; e se compadeceram dele e o consolaram por todo o mal que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} tinha trazido sobre ele; e cada um lhe deu uma quesita, e cada um, um anel de ouro.
pt.B: Todos os seus irmãos e irmãs e todos os que o tinham conhecido antes vieram e comeram com ele na sua casa. Eles se compadeceram dele e o consolaram por toda a desgraça que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} tinha trazido sobre ele, e cada um deles lhe deu {{units:uma peça de prata|uma quesita}} e um anel de ouro.
pt.R: Todos os seus irmãos e irmãs e todos os seus velhos amigos foram à casa dele e comeram com ele. Mostraram que se importavam com ele e o consolaram por todas as coisas difíceis que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} tinha trazido sobre ele. Cada um lhe deu {{units:uma peça de prata|uma quesita}} e um anel de ouro.

decisions.choice: the evil: the disaster, the trouble
decisions.reason: The word means harm or disaster as well as wickedness. It is the "evil" Job accepted from God in 2:10 and the "evil" the friends heard had come on him in 2:11; it is suffering, not sin.

decisions.choice: that the LORD had brought on him
decisions.reason: The narrator says what Job himself said (1:21; 2:10): the trouble came from the LORD. The Accuser of chapters 1-2 is not mentioned again; Job is never told of him.

decisions.choice: showed him sympathy and comforted him
decisions.reason: The same two verbs describe the friends' visit in 2:11. Now Job's family and old acquaintances, who had kept away from him (19:13-14), come and do what the friends set out to do.

decisions.choice: qesitah: a piece of money of unknown value
decisions.reason: The word is found elsewhere only in Genesis 33:19 and Joshua 24:32, where Jacob buys land for a hundred of them. It was probably a weight of silver; its value is not known.

decisions.choice: a piece of money, with "a qesitah" as the units setting (B, R)
decisions.reason: Since the value is unknown, Balanced and Readable describe it as a piece of money; the units setting gives the Hebrew name, which Literal keeps.

decisions.choice: 씩 outside the units span ("돈 한 닢" or "크시타 하나", then 씩과)
decisions.reason: 씩 attaches to both options alike, so one particle outside the span reads naturally with either setting.

decisions.choice: "o mal" (L), "a desgraça" (B), "as coisas difíceis" (R); "se compadeceram dele e o consolaram"; quesita, "uma peça de prata" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The evil is the one Job accepted from God in 2:10, and the two verbs are those of the friends' visit in 2:11 (m1, m3), so each level uses its own wording of those verses. The coin's name is spelled "quesita" as in the Portuguese of Genesis 33:19, whose Balanced also says "peças de prata" for it; "moeda" would suggest a minted coin, which m4 does not assume.

source.text: וַֽיהוָ֗ה בֵּרַ֛ךְ אֶת־אַחֲרִ֥ית אִיּ֖וֹב מֵרֵאשִׁת֑וֹ וַֽיְהִי־ל֡וֹ אַרְבָּעָה֩ עָשָׂ֨ר אֶ֜לֶף צֹ֗אן וְשֵׁ֤שֶׁת אֲלָפִים֙ גְּמַלִּ֔ים וְאֶֽלֶף־צֶ֥מֶד בָּקָ֖ר וְאֶ֥לֶף אֲתוֹנֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And the LORD blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning; and there were to him fourteen thousand sheep and six thousand camels and a thousand yoke of oxen and a thousand female donkeys.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} blessed the latter end of Job more than his beginning; and he had 14,000 sheep and 6,000 camels and 1,000 yoke of oxen and 1,000 female donkeys.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} blessed the last part of Job's life more than the first. He had 14,000 sheep, 6,000 camels, 1,000 yoke of oxen, and 1,000 female donkeys.
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} blessed Job even more in the last part of his life than in the first. He now had 14,000 sheep, 6,000 camels, 1,000 pairs of oxen, and 1,000 female donkeys.

es.L: Y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} bendijo el final de Job más que su principio; y tuvo 14 000 ovejas y 6000 camellos y 1000 yuntas de bueyes y 1000 asnas.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} bendijo la última parte de la vida de Job más que la primera. Tuvo 14 000 ovejas, 6000 camellos, 1000 yuntas de bueyes y 1000 asnas.
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} bendijo a Job en la última parte de su vida aún más que en la primera. Ahora tenía 14 000 ovejas, 6000 camellos, 1000 pares de bueyes y 1000 burras.

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} bénit la fin de Job plus que son commencement ; et il eut 14 000 moutons et 6 000 chameaux et 1 000 attelages de bœufs et 1 000 ânesses.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} bénit la dernière partie de la vie de Job plus que la première. Il eut 14 000 moutons, 6 000 chameaux, 1 000 paires de bœufs et 1 000 ânesses.
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a béni Job encore plus à la fin de sa vie qu’au début. Il avait maintenant 14 000 moutons, 6 000 chameaux, 1 000 paires de bœufs et 1 000 ânesses.

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akaubariki mwisho wa Ayubu kuliko mwanzo wake; akawa na kondoo 14,000 na ngamia 6,000 na jozi 1,000 za ng'ombe na punda wa kike 1,000.
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliibariki sehemu ya mwisho ya maisha ya Ayubu kuliko ile ya kwanza. Alikuwa na kondoo 14,000, ngamia 6,000, jozi 1,000 za ng'ombe na punda wa kike 1,000.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimbariki Ayubu zaidi katika miaka yake ya mwisho kuliko ile ya kwanza. Sasa alikuwa na kondoo 14,000, ngamia 6,000, jozi 1,000 za ng'ombe na punda wa kike 1,000.

vi.L: Và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ban phước cho cuối đời Gióp hơn lúc ban đầu; và ông có 14.000 chiên, 6.000 lạc đà, 1.000 cặp bò và 1.000 lừa cái.
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ban phước cho quãng đời sau của Gióp nhiều hơn quãng đời trước. Ông có 14.000 chiên, 6.000 lạc đà, 1.000 cặp bò và 1.000 lừa cái.
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ban phước cho Gióp trong những năm cuối đời còn nhiều hơn lúc trước. Giờ đây ông có 14.000 con chiên, 6.000 con lạc đà, 1.000 cặp bò và 1.000 con lừa cái.

ko.L: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 욥의 나중을 그의 처음보다 더 복되게 하셨다. 그는 양 14,000마리와 낙타 6,000마리와 소 1,000겨리와 암나귀 1,000마리를 가졌다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 욥의 생애 마지막을 처음보다 더 큰 복으로 채우셨다. 그는 양 14,000마리, 낙타 6,000마리, 소 1,000겨리, 암나귀 1,000마리를 가졌다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 욥의 인생 후반에 전보다 더 큰 복을 주셨다. 이제 그는 양 14,000마리, 낙타 6,000마리, 소 1,000쌍, 암나귀 1,000마리를 가지게 되었다.

pt.L: E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} abençoou o fim de Jó mais do que o seu princípio; e ele teve catorze mil ovelhas e seis mil camelos e mil juntas de bois e mil jumentas.
pt.B: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} abençoou o fim da vida de Jó mais do que o começo. Ele teve catorze mil ovelhas, seis mil camelos, mil juntas de bois e mil jumentas.
pt.R: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} abençoou Jó ainda mais na última parte da sua vida do que na primeira. Agora ele tinha catorze mil ovelhas, seis mil camelos, mil pares de bois e mil jumentas.

decisions.choice: blessed: real blessing
decisions.reason: Here the verb means to bless, not the "curse" it stands for in 1:5, 11 and 2:5, 9 (see the decision at 1:5). As in 1:21, it is true blessing.

decisions.choice: his latter end more than his beginning
decisions.reason: Bildad had told Job that if he were pure, "your beginning will seem small, and your latter end will grow very great" (8:7). The words come true, though not for Bildad's reasons.

decisions.choice: the numbers are double those of 1:3
decisions.reason: In 1:3 Job had 7,000 sheep, 3,000 camels, 500 yoke of oxen and 500 female donkeys. Each number is now doubled (42:10).

decisions.choice: pairs of oxen (R)
decisions.reason: A yoke of oxen is a pair harnessed together for plowing; Readable says "pairs".

decisions.choice: the numbers in words, as in 1:3 ("catorze mil ovelhas ... mil jumentas")
decisions.reason: The numbers are exactly double those of 1:3 (m3), which the Portuguese wrote in words ("sete mil ovelhas"); writing these in words too, with the same nouns at each level ("juntas de bois", R "pares de bois"; "jumentas"), lets the reader set the two lists side by side.

records.literal_gloss: And there were to him seven sons and three daughters.

en.L: And he had seven sons and three daughters.
en.B: He also had seven sons and three daughters.
en.R: He also had seven sons and three daughters.

es.L: Y tuvo siete hijos y tres hijas.
es.B: Tuvo también siete hijos y tres hijas.
es.R: También tuvo siete hijos y tres hijas.

fr.L: Et il eut sept fils et trois filles.
fr.B: Il eut aussi sept fils et trois filles.
fr.R: Il a eu aussi sept fils et trois filles.

sw.L: Akawa na wana saba wa kiume na binti watatu.
sw.B: Alikuwa pia na wana saba wa kiume na binti watatu.
sw.R: Pia alikuwa na watoto saba wa kiume na watatu wa kike.

vi.L: Và ông có bảy con trai và ba con gái.
vi.B: Ông cũng có bảy con trai và ba con gái.
vi.R: Ông cũng có bảy người con trai và ba người con gái.

ko.L: 그에게 아들 일곱과 딸 셋이 있었다.
ko.B: 그는 또 아들 일곱과 딸 셋을 두었다.
ko.R: 그는 또 아들 일곱 명과 딸 세 명을 두었다.

pt.L: E ele teve sete filhos e três filhas.
pt.B: Teve também sete filhos e três filhas.
pt.R: Ele também teve sete filhos e três filhas.

decisions.choice: seven
decisions.reason: The word for seven has an unusual ending here, and some take it to mean "twice seven", so that Job's sons were doubled like his flocks. But the plain sense is seven, and Job's three daughters are not doubled; the sons, like the daughters, are as many as in 1:2, while the flocks and herds are doubled (42:12).

source.text: וַיִּקְרָ֤א שֵׁם־הָֽאַחַת֙ יְמִימָ֔ה וְשֵׁ֥ם הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית קְצִיעָ֑ה וְשֵׁ֥ם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֖ית קֶ֥רֶן הַפּֽוּךְ׃

es.R: A su primera hija le puso por nombre Jemima; a la segunda, Cesia; y a la tercera, Queren-hapuc.

fr.B: Il nomma la première Yemima, la deuxième Qetsia et la troisième Qéren-Happouk.
fr.R: Il a appelé sa première fille Yemima, la deuxième Qetsia et la troisième Qéren-Happouk.

sw.R: Binti wa kwanza alimwita Yemima, wa pili Kezia, na wa tatu Keren-hapuki.

vi.L: Và ông gọi tên người thứ nhất là Giê-mi-ma, tên người thứ hai là Kê-xia, và tên người thứ ba là Kê-ren Ha-búc.
vi.B: Ông đặt tên cho người con gái đầu là Giê-mi-ma, người thứ hai là Kê-xia, người thứ ba là Kê-ren Ha-búc.
vi.R: Ông đặt tên cho con gái đầu lòng là Giê-mi-ma, con thứ hai là Kê-xia, và con thứ ba là Kê-ren Ha-búc.

ko.L: 그는 첫째의 이름을 여미마라 하고, 둘째의 이름을 긋시아라 하고, 셋째의 이름을 게렌합북이라 불렀다.
ko.B: 그는 첫째 딸을 여미마, 둘째를 긋시아, 셋째를 게렌합북이라고 이름 지었다.
ko.R: 그는 첫째 딸의 이름을 여미마라고 지었고, 둘째는 긋시아, 셋째는 게렌합북이라고 지었다.

pt.L: E chamou o nome da primeira Jemima, e o nome da segunda Quezia, e o nome da terceira Quéren-Hapuque.
pt.B: À primeira ele deu o nome de Jemima, à segunda, Quezia, e à terceira, Quéren-Hapuque.
pt.R: Ele deu à primeira filha o nome de Jemima, à segunda, o de Quezia, e à terceira, o de Quéren-Hapuque.

decisions.choice: the meaning of the daughters' names
decisions.reason: Jemimah probably means "dove"; Keziah is cassia, a fragrant spice (Psalm 45:9); Keren-happuch means "horn of eye paint", a container for the dark cosmetic women used around their eyes (2 Kings 9:30). All three names speak of beauty, as the next verse does.

decisions.choice: the daughters are named, the sons are not
decisions.reason: Hebrew stories usually name sons and leave daughters unnamed. Here only the daughters are named, which gives them special honor (42:15).

decisions.choice: Jemima, Quezia, Quéren-Hapuque
decisions.reason: The daughters' names in their usual Brazilian spelling, written as Portuguese writes the sounds, with no English "h" or "ch"; their meanings (m1) stay in the meaning note.

source.text: וְלֹ֨א נִמְצָ֜א נָשִׁ֥ים יָפ֛וֹת כִּבְנ֥וֹת אִיּ֖וֹב בְּכָל־הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיִּתֵּ֨ן לָהֶ֧ם אֲבִיהֶ֛ם נַחֲלָ֖ה בְּת֥וֹךְ אֲחֵיהֶֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And not were found women beautiful like [the] daughters of Job in all the land; and gave to them their father an inheritance among their brothers.

en.L: And there were not found women [as] beautiful as the daughters of Job in all the land; and their father gave them an inheritance among their brothers.
en.B: In all the land there were no women as beautiful as Job's daughters, and their father gave them an inheritance along with their brothers.
en.R: There were no women in the whole land as beautiful as Job's daughters. Their father gave them a share of his property, just as he did for their brothers.

es.L: Y no se hallaron mujeres [tan] hermosas como las hijas de Job en toda la tierra; y su padre les dio herencia entre sus hermanos.
es.B: En toda la tierra no había mujeres tan hermosas como las hijas de Job, y su padre les dio herencia junto con sus hermanos.
es.R: No había en todo el país mujeres tan hermosas como las hijas de Job. Su padre les dio una parte de sus bienes, igual que a sus hermanos.

fr.L: Et il ne se trouva pas de femmes [aussi] belles que les filles de Job dans tout le pays ; et leur père leur donna un héritage parmi leurs frères.
fr.B: Dans tout le pays, on ne trouvait pas de femmes aussi belles que les filles de Job, et leur père leur donna un héritage avec leurs frères.
fr.R: Dans tout le pays, il n’y avait pas de femmes aussi belles que les filles de Job. Leur père leur a donné une part de ses biens, comme à leurs frères.

sw.L: Wala hawakuonekana wanawake [walio] wazuri kama binti za Ayubu katika nchi yote; na baba yao akawapa urithi kati ya ndugu zao.
sw.B: Katika nchi yote hapakuwa na wanawake wazuri kama binti za Ayubu, na baba yao aliwapa urithi pamoja na ndugu zao wa kiume.
sw.R: Hapakuwa na wanawake katika nchi nzima waliokuwa wazuri kama binti za Ayubu. Baba yao aliwapa sehemu ya mali yake, kama alivyowapa ndugu zao wa kiume.

vi.L: Và trong khắp xứ không tìm được những người nữ [nào] đẹp như các con gái của Gióp; và cha họ cho họ cơ nghiệp giữa các anh em trai họ.
vi.B: Trong khắp xứ không có người nữ nào đẹp như các con gái của Gióp, và cha họ cho họ hưởng cơ nghiệp cùng với các anh em trai.
vi.R: Trong cả xứ không có phụ nữ nào đẹp bằng các con gái của Gióp. Cha họ chia cho họ một phần tài sản, giống như các anh em trai của họ.

ko.L: 온 땅에서 욥의 딸들처럼 아름다운 여자들을 찾을 수 없었다. 그리고 그들의 아버지는 그들에게 그들의 오라비들 가운데서 유업을 주었다.
ko.B: 온 땅에 욥의 딸들만큼 아름다운 여자가 없었다. 그들의 아버지는 그들에게도 오라비들과 함께 유산을 나누어 주었다.
ko.R: 온 나라에 욥의 딸들만큼 아름다운 여자는 없었다. 아버지는 딸들에게도 아들들에게 하듯이 재산을 나누어 주었다.

pt.L: E não se acharam mulheres [tão] belas como as filhas de Jó em toda a terra; e o pai delas lhes deu herança entre os seus irmãos.
pt.B: Em toda a terra não havia mulheres tão bonitas como as filhas de Jó, e o pai lhes deu herança junto com os irmãos delas.
pt.R: Não havia em toda aquela terra mulheres tão bonitas como as filhas de Jó. O pai deu a elas uma parte dos seus bens, assim como deu aos irmãos delas.

decisions.choice: an inheritance among their brothers: the daughters inherit with the sons
decisions.reason: In Israel's law daughters inherited their father's land only when there were no sons (Numbers 27:1-11). Job gives his daughters a share alongside their brothers, a sign of his wealth and of his love for them.

decisions.choice: a share of his property (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what the inheritance was.

source.text: וַיְחִ֤י אִיּוֹב֙ אַֽחֲרֵי־זֹ֔את מֵאָ֥ה וְאַרְבָּעִ֖ים שָׁנָ֑ה וַיִּרְאֶ֗ה אֶת־בָּנָיו֙ וְאֶת־בְּנֵ֣י בָנָ֔יו אַרְבָּעָ֖ה דֹּרֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And lived Job after this a hundred and forty years, and saw his sons and [the] sons of his sons, four generations.

en.L: And Job lived after this 140 years, and saw his {{gender:children|sons}} and his {{gender:children's children|sons' sons}}, four generations.
en.B: After this Job lived 140 years, and he saw his {{gender:children and grandchildren|sons and grandsons}} to the fourth generation.
en.R: After this, Job lived 140 more years. He lived to see his {{gender:children, grandchildren, and great-grandchildren|sons, grandsons, and great-grandsons}}, and their children too: four generations.

es.L: Y vivió Job después de esto 140 años, y vio a sus hijos y a los hijos de sus hijos, cuatro generaciones.
es.B: Después de esto Job vivió 140 años, y vio a sus hijos y a sus nietos hasta la cuarta generación.
es.R: Después de esto, Job vivió 140 años más. Llegó a ver a sus hijos, a sus nietos, a sus bisnietos y a los hijos de estos: cuatro generaciones.

fr.L: Et Job vécut après cela 140 ans, et il vit ses {{gender:enfants|fils}} et les {{gender:enfants de ses enfants|fils de ses fils}}, quatre générations.
fr.B: Après cela, Job vécut 140 ans, et il vit ses {{gender:enfants et ses petits-enfants|fils et ses petits-fils}} jusqu’à la quatrième génération.
fr.R: Après cela, Job a vécu encore 140 ans. Il a vu ses {{gender:enfants, ses petits-enfants et ses arrière-petits-enfants|fils, ses petits-fils et ses arrière-petits-fils}}, et leurs enfants aussi : quatre générations.

sw.L: Na Ayubu akaishi baada ya hayo miaka 140, akawaona wana wake na wana wa wana wake, vizazi vinne.
sw.B: Baada ya hayo Ayubu aliishi miaka 140, akawaona watoto wake na wajukuu wake hadi kizazi cha nne.
sw.R: Baada ya hayo, Ayubu aliishi miaka mingine 140. Aliwaona watoto wake, wajukuu wake, vitukuu vyake na watoto wao pia: vizazi vinne.

vi.L: Và sau việc ấy Gióp sống 140 năm, và thấy {{gender:con cái|các con trai}} mình và {{gender:con cái của con cái|các con trai của con trai}} mình, bốn đời.
vi.B: Sau việc ấy, Gióp sống thêm 140 năm và thấy {{gender:con cháu|con trai và cháu trai}} mình đến đời thứ tư.
vi.R: Sau đó Gióp sống thêm 140 năm nữa. Ông được thấy {{gender:con, cháu, chắt|con trai, cháu trai, chắt trai}} của mình, và cả con của chúng nữa: bốn thế hệ.

ko.L: 이 후에 욥은 140년을 살았고, 그의 {{gender:자녀들|아들들}}과 {{gender:자녀들의 자녀들|아들들의 아들들}}, 곧 사 대를 보았다.
ko.B: 그 뒤에 욥은 140년을 살면서 {{gender:자녀와 손주들|아들과 손자들}}을 사 대까지 보았다.
ko.R: 그 뒤로 욥은 140년을 더 살았다. 그는 {{gender:자녀와 손주와 증손주들|아들과 손자와 증손자들}}과 그들의 자녀까지, 네 세대를 보았다.

pt.L: E Jó viveu depois disso cento e quarenta anos, e viu os seus filhos e os filhos dos seus filhos, quatro gerações.
pt.B: Depois disso Jó viveu cento e quarenta anos e viu os seus filhos e netos até a quarta geração.
pt.R: Depois disso, Jó viveu mais cento e quarenta anos. Chegou a ver os seus filhos, netos e bisnetos, e os filhos deles também: quatro gerações.

decisions.choice: seeing four generations: the blessing of a long life
decisions.reason: To live to see one's grandchildren and their children was a mark of God's blessing (Genesis 50:23; Psalm 128:6; Proverbs 17:6). Eliphaz had promised Job many descendants if he accepted God's correction (5:25).

decisions.choice: his sons: his children, daughters as well as sons
decisions.reason: The word means sons, but in a phrase like "his sons and his sons' sons" it means descendants of both sexes, and Job's daughters have just been named (42:14-15).

decisions.choice: and he saw (as read)
decisions.reason: The written text and the scribes' reading note spell the verb slightly differently; both mean "and he saw".

decisions.choice: children, grandchildren, and great-grandchildren, and their children too (R)
alternatives: his sons and his sons' sons, four generations
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the four generations.

decisions.choice: no gender span: "hijos", "nietos", "bisnietos"
alternatives: a span as in the English
decisions.reason: Spanish "hijos" and "nietos" already cover daughters as well as sons (m2), so the setting would change nothing.

decisions.choice: "filhos", "netos", "bisnetos" with no gender span
alternatives: filhos e filhas, netos e netas
decisions.reason: The English puts "children|sons" under the gender setting because English "sons" excludes daughters. Portuguese "filhos", "netos" and "bisnetos" already include daughters and granddaughters (m2; docs/pentateuch-portuguese-terms.md), so both options would read the same and no setting is used.

records.literal_gloss: And died Job, old and full of days.

en.L: And Job died, old and full of days.
en.B: And Job died, old and satisfied with his days.
en.R: Then Job died. He was very old and had lived a long, full life.

es.L: Y murió Job, viejo y lleno de días.
es.B: Y Job murió, anciano y satisfecho de sus días.
es.R: Luego Job murió. Era muy anciano y había tenido una vida larga y plena.

fr.L: Et Job mourut, vieux et plein de jours.
fr.B: Puis Job mourut, âgé et comblé de jours.
fr.R: Ensuite Job est mort. Il était très âgé et avait vécu une longue vie bien remplie.

sw.L: Kisha Ayubu akafa, mzee na aliyeshiba siku.
sw.B: Ayubu akafa akiwa mzee, ameridhika na siku zake.
sw.R: Kisha Ayubu akafa. Alikuwa mzee sana, na alikuwa ameishi maisha marefu yenye kuridhisha.

vi.L: Và Gióp chết, già nua và no đủ ngày tháng.
vi.B: Rồi Gióp qua đời, tuổi cao và mãn nguyện với những ngày đời mình.
vi.R: Sau đó Gióp qua đời. Ông đã rất già và đã sống một cuộc đời dài và trọn vẹn.

ko.B: 욥은 늙어서 자기 생애에 만족하며 죽었다.
ko.R: 그 후 욥은 죽었다. 그는 아주 오래 살았고, 길고 넉넉한 삶을 누렸다.

pt.L: E Jó morreu, velho e farto de dias.
pt.B: E Jó morreu velho e farto de dias.
pt.R: Então Jó morreu. Ele estava muito velho e tinha vivido uma vida longa e completa.

decisions.choice: old and full of days: having lived a long and complete life
decisions.reason: The same words are said of Abraham (Genesis 25:8), Isaac (Genesis 35:29) and David (1 Chronicles 29:28). The word "full" means satisfied: Job dies having had all the life he could wish, like the great men of old.

decisions.choice: satisfied with his days (B); had lived a long, full life (R)
decisions.reason: "Full" is the word for being satisfied with food; Balanced brings out that sense, and Readable says what the phrase means (m1).

decisions.choice: velho e farto de dias (L, B); "uma vida longa e completa" (R)
alternatives: idoso e satisfeito com os seus anos (B)
decisions.reason: The same words close the lives of Abraham and Isaac (Genesis 25:8; 35:29; m1); the Portuguese of Genesis 35:29 says "farto de dias" at Literal, and its Readable "uma vida longa e completa", so Job's death is told in those words. Balanced keeps "farto de dias" too: "farto" is the Portuguese word for being full after a meal, which carries the sense of satisfaction the English Balanced brings out.
